observations.behavior: Removes several account fields (funding_source_details, is_prepay_account, tos_accepted, owner) and their associated comments.
observations.posthog_connection: These fields require the 'business_management' OAuth scope which PostHog's current Meta Ads integration does not request; including them would cause API requests to fail with 400 errors, breaking warehouse ingestion.

observations.behavior: Adds an error message distinguishing between generic re-authentication failures and specific permission-denied responses requiring support intervention rather than user-side re-authorisation.
observations.posthog_connection: Clarifies operational behavior for users encountering this specific failure mode during warehouse syncs, preventing unnecessary re-authorization attempts that cannot resolve the issue.

observations.behavior: Adds test assertions verifying these four fields are excluded from account listing field names.
observations.posthog_connection: Provides regression protection against accidentally including business-gated fields in future schema changes or configuration updates.

observations.limitations: Only three hunks reviewed. No score assigned because tier assignment requires broader context: while P1.F1.H1 removes problematic fields, it is unclear whether other parts of the codebase still attempt to include them elsewhere, nor if there are additional compatibility considerations. The removal alone could be narrow maintenance without systemic benefit.

review.posthog_relevance: Relevant to PostHog's Meta Ads warehouse integration; fixes potential 400 errors when syncing account data, improving reliability of warehouse ingestion workflows.
review.uncertainty: Could this be considered Tier 1? It could also qualify as Tier 3 if similar permission issues exist widely across other warehouse sources—but no such evidence exists here.
